title: Autonomous agents: what runs an agent when no one is in the conversation?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the trigger mechanics, credential models, billing and governance controls. The corrected enforcement statement preserves both the pay-as-you-go exception and the administrator-off and stop-usage restrictions.

claims.claim: Autonomous agents in Copilot Studio act without waiting for a user prompt.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio can act without waiting for a user prompt.

claims.claim: A schedule can start an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: Administrators can use data policies to prevent makers from adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: Administrators can govern the use of maker credentials.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting in the Power Platform admin center to prevent agents from being shared when they contain connections configured to use maker credentials that other users aren't permitted to reuse.

claims.claim: Administrators can control agent consumption.
claims.quote: Set agent limits: Set limits on how much an agent can spend. An agent must consume some credits before you can set limits.

claims.claim: Event-driven execution does not mean the agent runs continuously.
claims.quote: Event-driven execution doesn't mean the agent runs continuously.

claims.quote: If the tenant is already at 125% Copilot Credit consumption because of Environment B and Environment C, enforcement isn't placed on the agents in Environment A, as long as Environment A has remaining capacity from its allocation of 10,000 Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <PolicyGuid> -Classification Blocked -Connectors <ConnectorObjects> moves connector objects into the policy's Blocked group.

Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>

    [-Connectors] <Object[]>

Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.where: controls[1].scope; controls[1].note; Governance controls: Sharing rule

claims.claim: The sharing rule uses solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode in governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings.
claims.quote: $governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode' -Value "disableSharing" -Force

claims.claim: The disableSharing value turns off solution-aware cloud flow sharing.
claims.quote:
Here's a PowerShell script that turns off sharing for solution-aware cloud flows.

$governanceConfiguration.settings.extendedSettings | Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode' -Value "disableSharing" -Force

claims.claim: Let people share solution-aware cloud flows governs sharing of both solution-aware cloud flows and agent flows.
